verdicts.title: One limiter charge pipeline: reserve the caller slot before the store await
verdicts.ambition_why: Closes a real TOCTOU on the production (shared-store) path and collapses two copies of the QUOTA rules into one pipeline that owns its telemetry; a principal's move, not a tidy-up.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every anchor re-verified: checkWindow at rate-limit.ts:223, the await at :236, admit() records after it, recordHit's own comment at rate-limit-window.ts:181-182, the three hand-placed recordQuotaEvent sites, the peek mislabel at scan/route.ts:116, the unavailable-counted-as-trip at scan-gates.ts:76, rateLimiterStats read by nothing, zero concurrent cases in the 968-line rate-limit.test.ts.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Case 1 (25 concurrent with a 20ms store fake -> 25 ok today) is red by construction; cases 3-6 pin kinds/scopes a wrong build would get wrong; case 7 is a repo-wide grep that pins the single-owner property.
verdicts.notes: POLICY CHECK (as asked): no limit raised or removed, no window changed, fail-closed default and ASCENT_RATE_LIMIT_SHARED_FAIL_OPEN untouched; reserve->charge global->commit/release is semantically identical to today's check->charge->record on every sequential path (QUOTA #1/#3 preserved), so nothing in the card loosens policy. The only observable change is telemetry: a new QuotaEventKind 'rate_limit_unavailable' (must stay OUT of ABUSE_KINDS, which the guard pins) and new '<limiter>:global' scope strings on the /usage rateLimitTrips series (additive rows, consumed only by this repo's panel). Builder notes: (a) the existing 429 JSON body and retry-after headers are consumed by external CI via the gate route and must stay byte-identical (the card keeps tooManyRequests untouched, keep it so); (b) gate-order.test.ts mocks recordQuotaEvent at the route level, the moved assertion must stay in that file or a route-level 'scan' event regression goes unobserved. Impact 7 not 8: the race only exists when a shared store is configured (ASCENT_RATE_LIMIT_SHARED_* set), which is the production posture but not the default. Write-set overlap with RUN 5 (22e) 'A scan credit reservation is a keyed ledger object' on src/lib/scan-gates.ts and src/app/api/org/import/route.ts: serialize after it, the touches here are 2-3 lines each.

verdicts.title: A throttled scan counts down its Retry-After and resumes itself
verdicts.ambition_why: A missing client mode that uses a contract the server already publishes; useful and correct, but a bounded UX fill rather than a structural move.
verdicts.grounding_why: useReportScan.ts:312 classifies only monthly_quota, :339-341 settles every other 429 as a generic error, ReportRescanAlert.tsx:21-23 treats a throttle as transient (Retry), ReportClientEmpty.tsx:44-45 'Try again' -> fresh=1, stream/route.ts:74-75 returns the whole limiter result as JSON, grep for rate_limited/rate_limit_unavailable in src/components is empty.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Pure-model cases (parse per scope, jitter via injected rng, two-resume cap, hidden-tab pause) are deterministic and red before; the dom case with fake timers pins 'exactly once'. Case 8 (re-test keeps the report mounted) depends on the hook wiring and is the one a wrong build could pass by accident if retest() is stubbed.
verdicts.notes: POLICY CHECK: pure client; no limit, window, fail-open/closed or server change; monthly_quota (402/401) paths untouched by parseThrottle returning null. Auto-resume is bounded (2 per visit, never from a hidden tab) and the limiter runs before the quota consume (scan-gates.ts:40-41 verified), so a resume cannot burn a free slot. Builder note: a resumed FIRST scan must re-issue the same /api/scan/stream request (nothing was cached by a throttled attempt), not navigate to fresh=1. Impact 6: at 20/min/IP the per-IP throttle is rare for a human; the win is mostly on the global/unavailable scopes where the copy stops blaming the visitor. No file overlap with run 4/5 cards (22d touches ReportHeader/ReportView/BriefingComposer, 22c touched other report components and is landed).

verdicts.title: The migration chain builds the schema: 26 unmigrated tables caught up, converge
verdicts.revise: Acceptance case 5 becomes the exact no-op proof for an EXISTING, fully-migrated database and is the gating case: build a PGlite store from prisma/init.sql (the shape every deployed DB has), take the normalized dump {tables, columns(type,nullability,default), index names+defs}, exec BOTH catch-up migrations TWICE (idempotency), and assert the dump is byte-identical after each pass; the same two files must also replay cleanly on a store built from the full chain (case 1 already covers fresh). Any statement form without a native IF NOT EXISTS (there are no FOREIGN KEYs in init.sql, so this means only ALTER COLUMN SET DEFAULT or constraint adds) is forbidden in the catch-ups: the additivity grep in case 6 must also reject 'SET DEFAULT' and 'ADD CONSTRAINT'.
verdicts.ambition_why: Makes the documented self-host and production road (vercel.json buildCommand, SELF-HOSTING.md:114) actually work and adds the convergence guard that stops the drift recurring; the registry's 'two roads, one schema' standard applied.
verdicts.grounding_why: Re-derived on the tree: 26 of 89 models have no CREATE TABLE in any of the 82 migrations (same 26 names), 20260831120000 ALTERs LaneItemOutcome which only init.sql:2375 creates, 20260923120000 ALTERs RepoConformanceMap (init.sql:2038), init-sql.test.ts compares only schema<->init.sql, pglite-boot.ts:33 boots from init.sql, 8 updatedAt/lastSeen DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP columns in init.sql (card says 7; QuotaEvent.lastSeen is @updatedAt in schema, the builder's chain diff decides the exact set).
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cases 1-3 are measured red today (the replay halts at 0831); case 4 seeds a violation into the matcher; case 5 (as revised) is the no-op proof the parent demanded; case 6 pins additivity against a future cleanup.
verdicts.notes: RULING ON THE BACK-DATED MIGRATION: `prisma migrate deploy` (prisma 6.19.3) applies every folder not present in _prisma_migrations in name order and does not check ordering or drift, so on an existing production DB that has applied all 82 steps, 20260831115900_* and 20261023130000_* are simply two pending steps run on the next deploy. They are safe iff they are pure CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS / CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX IF NOT EXISTS / ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, which the tree permits (init.sql carries zero FOREIGN KEY constraints by DSQL design, so every statement the catch-up needs has a native IF NOT EXISTS form). The revised case 5 is the proof the builder can run without a Postgres. Two things the card cannot fix and should NOT claim to: (1) the P3005 history (memory: master-ci-red-causes) means production may never have been baselined; a DB baselined only on 0_init would then run all 81 later steps including non-IF-NOT-EXISTS ALTERs on columns that already exist and fail on the first one, a PRE-EXISTING hazard this card neither worsens nor repairs, and DEPLOY.md must say so rather than imply db:deploy now works on such a DB; (2) data-model.md:393-399 documents the init.sql-only road as a 'Migration convention followed' for the #18 tables, so the doc edit must retire that paragraph (it is a known-gap-stated-as-convention; leaving it contradicts the new guard). Dropping the 7-8 DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP clauses from init.sql is safe on the tree: no raw INSERT into those tables exists in src/ or scripts/, Prisma sets @updatedAt itself, and existing PGlite data dirs keep the default (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS skips them). Catch-up 2 must sort after run 4's 20261023120000_mentor_share_org_aggregate (20261023130000 does) and the chain test will also police run 4's and run 5's new migrations (20261024090000_org_logo_snapshot), which must carry their own DDL. WRITE-SET OVERLAP with RUN 5 (22e) 'The logo is a validated asset snapshotted at save' on prisma/init.sql: serialize. Size L and risk 7 are at the floor's edge but honest.

verdicts.title: Auth-expiry self-heal moves into the client: 131 raw getPrisma files recover
verdicts.revise: Scope the extension so the two parent rulings hold by construction, with a test against a REAL PrismaClient, not only the fake: (a) the $allOperations hook refuses to recover when its params carry a transaction (Prisma passes `__internalParams.transaction` for both interactive and batch $transaction operations; the tree has 31 interactive and 5 batch call sites that client.ts cannot wrap), and (b) recovery is limited to the idempotent read operations (findUnique, findUniqueOrThrow, findFirst, findFirstOrThrow, findMany, count, aggregate, groupBy); create/update/upsert/delete/*Many keep today's opt-in withDb door, because isAuthExpiryError also matches by message ('access denied', 'token'+'expired') and a message-classified error after the statement reached the server would replay a write. Case 4 must run over the PGlite adapter client (`$transaction(async tx => tx.x.findMany())` with an injected auth-shaped throw) so the test proves what Prisma actually passes, and the source guard in case 7 stays.
verdicts.ambition_why: Invariant placement at the single construction point is the right instinct; the card's actual lever (every write self-heals too) is where it overreaches.
verdicts.grounding_why: Counts reproduced exactly on the tree: 152 non-test getPrisma files, 131 with none of dbReadSafe/dbReadStrict/withDb(/runWithReconnect, 20 dbReadSafe files; client.ts:318 comment, :325/:372/:775 wrappers, :536 newClient single construction point, :678 getPrisma sync return, :746 runWithReconnect; `$extends` absent from src.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cases 1-3, 5-7 are red before and pin once-only recovery, but case 4 (no replay inside a transaction) is only as true as the fake client's simulation of Prisma's params; without a real-client run it can be green while the production hook replays a tx statement on another connection.
verdicts.notes: RULING (as asked): as written the card does not prove either invariant. The AsyncLocalStorage fence only de-duplicates dbReadSafe's own recovery; it cannot know a caller is inside $transaction because $transaction is not a query operation and the 36 call sites are outside the write set, so the stated 'inside an interactive transaction it rethrows' has no named mechanism. Replaying a query on a fresh client from inside an itx escapes the transaction (the itx connection is dead, the replay commits or reads outside it, the enclosing tx later fails at commit): harmless for a read, a torn write for a mutation. On idempotency: an auth failure at CONNECT time means the statement never ran, so replaying even a write is safe for the code-matched classes (28000/28P01/P1000/P1010), but the message-matched tail of isAuthExpiryError is broad enough that a once-only replay of a non-idempotent write cannot be proven never to double-execute; restricting the heal to reads keeps the 131-file win where it matters (the read surface the docs claim is covered) and leaves writes on the explicit door. Impact 5 not 7: getPrisma already kicks a proactive refresh inside the margin (:684), so the reactive path fires only on a cold thaw or a mint stall. No write-set overlap with run 4/5 cards. Note client.ts is 843 lines (no cap, .ts) and the runner-up split is the better long-term home; not required here.

verdicts.title: One Scan-row codec: every persisted report column decodes back onto the report
verdicts.ambition_why: Replaces two hand-lists with one declared codec and a completeness guard, fixing five silently-dropped fields on every reconstructed report (DB-tier cache, permalink, foundation PR, lane install); the row-mapping technique applied, not a rename.
verdicts.grounding_why: scans-persist.ts:525/542/547/551/555 write the five columns; scans-read.ts has zero hits for contextHealth/guidanceGraph/practiceShape and platformSignals only at 595/644/672 and 1050-1095, none inside loadScanReportByCommit (1369-1568); org-rollup.ts:858-860 decodes the same blobs off Repository; scan-cache.ts:188-191 warms the memory tier with the reconstructed report; manifest.ts:323 reads report.manifest and :58/:79 guidanceGraph; stack.ts:94, skill.ts:218, lane-install.ts:122 all verified.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cases 1-2 are red today (fields undefined), case 3 pins ABSENT vs empty, case 4 pins corrupt-JSON tolerance, case 5 is a tsc-level round-trip, case 6 fails on any column written without a decode decision, case 7 is an end-to-end observable (manifest.yaml carries `npm test`).
verdicts.notes: Gate 'contract' is right: what getScanReportByCommit returns gains five fields. Builder notes: (a) the persist-side comments at scans-persist.ts:540-555 say 'Null on a reconstructed snapshot', which this card makes false; update them in the same change; (b) encode output must stay byte-identical (scans-persist.test.ts:488-630 asserts the strings); (c) the new fields on a DB-tier cache hit flow into persistedMatchesActiveIdentity and the memory tier, which is the intended effect, but loadComparableScan's select (:644) must not be widened beyond platformSignalsJson or the comparison query gets heavier for nothing. OVERLAPS: within this run with scan-persist B on src/lib/db/scans-persist.ts (different regions: the scan.create block vs the carry loop; serialize A then B). With RUN 5 (22e) 'One public-corpus door' (revise) on src/lib/db/scans-read.ts: serialize. Run 4's 'One report-export read door' reads getScanReportByCommit and will inherit the five fields, a semantic coupling, not a file overlap.

verdicts.title: Carry-forward as a pure plan: no kept in-progress claim vanishes on rescan
verdicts.ambition_why: Lifts a hidden state machine out of a retried transaction into a pure plan addressed by index, fixing two keep reasons that silently drop a user's claim today; the unit-of-work technique applied where the ledger's trust lives.
verdicts.grounding_why: followups.ts:145 (restated short-circuit), :173 mock-scan, :177 within-noise, keepNote returns a note for both (:206-208, :219-220); scans-persist.ts:437 hand-lists exactly no-movement/craft-unclaimed/rubric-changed, :441-443 pushes the rest paired:true, :651-654 findFirst by the OLD title, :676 `if (!target) continue`, three row copies at 589/619/656, commit 50974709 is the prior field-drift fix, scans-persist.test.ts has no within-noise/mock-scan case.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cases 1-2 are red today (row vanishes), case 3 is red (note dropped on a normalized-title restatement), case 4 is a table test over the whole reason union so a new reason cannot land in the wrong branch, case 5 enumerates the select's fields against the copier, case 6 pins purity and closedFollowUpIds == plan.resolved.
verdicts.notes: Correctness fix on the Follow-ups ledger with no schema change and a clean rollback. Builder notes: (a) case 3 addresses the paired keep by the NEW row's roadmap index, which requires the transaction to collect created ids in roadmap order (createMany returns no ids; keep the per-row create or map back by index after a select); (b) planCarryForward must be computed BEFORE withRetry opens the transaction, as the body says, so a replay cannot re-derive a different plan; (c) the doc is docs/features/org-followups/README.md and the ledger wording for within-noise/mock-scan already exists in keepNote, so no copy changes. OVERLAP: with scan-persist A on src/lib/db/scans-persist.ts (serialize). No overlap with run 4/5 cards; run 2 (22b) 'Status-transition consequences in one module' touched this file and is landed, so the line anchors here are post-landing and verified.
